en.headline:

selling books to Anthropic
en.body: A Nippan subsidiary sold Japanese books to Anthropic from Dec 2024 to Dec 2025 without telling publishers.

blocks.cap: From U.S. court documents: a view inside a warehouse where a large volume of collected books are believed to be stored

blocks.x: A subsidiary of major book distributor Nippan Group Holdings, Inc. has sold Japanese books to U.S. artificial intelligence developer Anthropic PBC without notifying the publishers. The Japan Book Publishers Association inquired about the matter and received a response from Nippan confirming the sales, according to publishing industry sources.

Anthropic is believed to have been conducting a project to scan large quantities of books for AI training, and Japanese books may have been included. According to court documents, Anthropic had been purchasing large quantities of books from distributors in Europe, the United States and Asia, among them a company named “Nippan Japan.”

The association demanded that Nippan cease the supply and sale of books intended for AI training. Nippan reportedly acknowledged sales between December 2024 and December 2025, but claimed it was not aware the books were being purchased for AI training.

Article 30-4 of Japan’s Copyright Law permits the use of works for AI training without permission, unless it unreasonably prejudices the copyright owner’s interests. A senior publishing executive said: “It is unacceptable for Nippan, which is in a position to protect Japan’s publishing culture, to engage in actions that undermine that very culture.”

cards.headline:
스페인 자가출판 히트작
30%, 대부분 AI 작성

blocks.cap: 바르셀로나의 한 서점에서 직원이 고전 코너를 살핀다.

blocks.x: EL PAÍS는 Amazon.es와 Casa del Libro 베스트셀러 목록, 주요 문학상에서 2025년과 2026년에 나온 인기 도서 119권을 골라 탐지 도구 Pangram으로 분석했다. 같은 방식으로 2019년과 2020년에 나온 책 56권을 살펴보니 AI 생성 흔적은 하나도 없었다. 모두 0%였다.
최근 도서 119권 중 35권(29%)에서 AI-generated 텍스트 흔적이 일부 보였고 13권은 50%를 넘었다. AI를 쓴 책은 자가출판 쪽에 몰렸다. 자가출판 도서 44권 중 13권으로 30%였고, 상당수가 로맨스 소설이었다. Javier Cercas, Isabel Allende, Dolores Redondo 같은 기성 작가의 책은 0%였다.
가장 눈에 띄는 사례는 스페인 정치인 Alvise Pérez의 Devuélveme mi país다. 2026년 이월 Amazon에서 No. 1에 오른 이 책을 두고 Pangram은 내용의 97%를 AI가 썼다고 판정했다. Pérez는 “한 단어 한 단어” 직접 썼다고 말했다.
전통 방식으로 나온 책 가운데서도 아홉 권에서 AI 흔적이 일부 발견됐다. 그중 논픽션 네 권은 12%에서 34% 사이였다. Pangram이 완벽하지는 않다. 작업 과정에서 사람이 어떤 역할을 했는지도 가려내지 못한다.

en.headline:
30% of Spain's self-published
hits are mostly written by AI
en.body: EL PAÍS found no AI in 56 books from 2019–20, but 13 of 44 recent self-published bestsellers scored above 50%.

blocks.cap: A bookstore clerk in Barcelona checks the classics section.

blocks.x: EL PAÍS examined 119 popular books published in 2025 and 2026, from the Amazon.es and Casa del Libro bestseller lists and major literary prizes, using the Pangram detection tool. The same exercise on 56 books from 2019 and 2020 found no signs of AI generation: all scored 0%.

Of the 119 recent titles, 35 showed some evidence of AI-generated text (29%) and 13 scored above 50%. AI use was concentrated in self-published works: 13 of 44, or 30%, many of them romance novels. Established authors such as Javier Cercas, Isabel Allende and Dolores Redondo scored 0%.

The most prominent case is Devuélveme mi país by Spanish politician Alvise Pérez, which reached No. 1 on Amazon in February 2026; Pangram attributes 97% of it to AI. Pérez said he wrote the book “word for word.”

Nine traditionally published books showed some traces of AI, including four nonfiction works scoring 12% to 34%. Pangram is not infallible, and it cannot reveal what role a person played in the process.

cards.headline:

AI 투명성 호소에 동참
cards.body: Frankfurt Appeal은 EU와 독일에 AI 학습 작품 공개를 요구한다.

blocks.x: 150곳이 넘는 출판사와 출판 단체가 EU와 독일 정부에 AI 개발사가 모델 학습에 쓴 작품을 공개하도록 의무화하라고 촉구한다. 요구 내용은 독일출판서점협회가 발표한 Frankfurt Appeal에 담겼다.
호소문은 세 가지를 요구한다. 작품 단위로 학습 데이터를 공개하는 투명성 의무, 공정한 수익 모델을 갖춘 라이선스 시장, 강력한 집행 수단이 뒷받침하는 유럽 저작권법 준수다. “침해해도 아무 결과가 따르지 않는 권리는 무가치하다.”
협회장 Sebastian Guggolz는 “정치권이 지금 행동하지 않으면 AI는 계속해서 수백만 편의 저작물을 빼앗고, 결국에는 우리의 사고 능력까지 빼앗을 것”이라고 말했다.

2026년 시월 9일 현재 Suhrkamp, Hanser, Rowohlt, Carlsen, Penguin Random House Verlagsgruppe, Diogenes, International Publishers Association, Federation of European Publishers를 비롯해 브라질, 이집트, UK, 오스트리아, 네덜란드, 아르헨티나, 태국, 호주의 출판사까지 150곳 넘는 단체가 서명했다.

en.headline:
Over 150 publishing groups
back an AI transparency appeal
en.body: The Frankfurt Appeal asks the EU and Germany to make AI developers disclose the works used to train their models.

blocks.x: More than 150 publishers and publishing organizations are urging the EU and the German government to require AI developers to disclose the works used to train their models. The demand is outlined in the Frankfurt Appeal, published by the German Publishers and Booksellers Association.

The appeal calls for three actions: transparency obligations including disclosure of training data at work level; a licensing market with fair revenue models; and compliance with European copyright law, equipped with robust means of enforcement. “Rights whose infringement carries no consequences are worthless.”
“If politicians do not act now, AI will continue to deprive us of millions of copyrighted works and, eventually, of our ability to think,” said association head Sebastian Guggolz.

As of Oct. 9, 2026, more than 150 organizations had signed, including Suhrkamp, Hanser, Rowohlt, Carlsen, Penguin Random House Verlagsgruppe, Diogenes, the International Publishers Association and the Federation of European Publishers, plus publishers from Brazil, Egypt, the UK, Austria, the Netherlands, Argentina, Thailand and Australia.

AI透明性の訴えに賛同
ja.body: Frankfurt AppealはEUとドイツにAI開発者へ学習作品の開示義務化を求める。

blocks.x: 150を超える出版社と出版団体が、EUとドイツ政府に対し、AI開発者にモデルの学習に使った作品の開示を義務づけるよう求めている。この要求は、ドイツ出版・書店協会が公表したFrankfurt Appealにまとめられている。
アピールは三つの行動を求めている。作品単位での学習データ開示を含む透明性義務、公正な収益モデルを備えたライセンス市場、そして強力な執行手段を伴う欧州著作権法の順守だ。「侵害しても何の報いもない権利に価値はない」。
協会のSebastian Guggolz会長は「政治が今動かなければ、AIは私たちから何百万もの著作物を、そしてやがては考える力さえも奪い続けるだろう」と述べた。

2026年十月9日時点で、Suhrkamp、Hanser、Rowohlt、Carlsen、Penguin Random House Verlagsgruppe、Diogenes、International Publishers Association、Federation of European Publishersのほか、ブラジル、エジプト、UK、オーストリア、オランダ、アルゼンチン、タイ、オーストラリアの出版社を含む150以上の団体が署名した。

zh.headline:

联署AI透明度呼吁

呼吁书提出三项行动：包括在作品层面公开训练数据在内的透明度义务；具备公平收益模式的授权市场；以及遵守欧洲著作权法，并配备有力的执行手段。“侵权而无须承担后果的权利毫无价值。”
协会负责人Sebastian Guggolz表示：“如果政界现在不采取行动，AI将继续夺走我们数以百万计的受版权保护作品，最终还会夺走我们的思考能力。”

截至2026年十月9日，已有150多家机构签署，包括Suhrkamp、Hanser、Rowohlt、Carlsen、Penguin Random House Verlagsgruppe、Diogenes、International Publishers Association和Federation of European Publishers，以及来自巴西、埃及、UK、奥地利、荷兰、阿根廷、泰国和澳大利亚的出版商。

Más de 150 grupos editoriales
piden transparencia en la AI
es.body: El Frankfurt Appeal pide a la EU y a Alemania que los desarrolladores de AI revelen las obras con las que entrenan.
es.mini_headline: El Frankfurt Appeal por la transparencia en AI

blocks.x: Más de 150 editoriales y organizaciones del sector instan a la EU y al Gobierno alemán a obligar a los desarrolladores de AI a revelar las obras usadas para entrenar sus modelos. La petición se recoge en el Frankfurt Appeal, publicado por la Asociación Alemana de Editores y Libreros.

El llamamiento pide tres medidas: obligaciones de transparencia que incluyan la divulgación de los datos de entrenamiento obra por obra; un mercado de licencias con modelos de ingresos justos; y el cumplimiento de la legislación europea de derechos de autor, con mecanismos sólidos para hacerla valer. “Los derechos cuya infracción no tiene consecuencias no valen nada”.

“Si los políticos no actúan ahora, la AI seguirá privándonos de millones de obras protegidas por derechos de autor y, con el tiempo, de nuestra capacidad de pensar”, afirmó Sebastian Guggolz, presidente de la asociación.

A 9 de octubre de 2026, más de 150 organizaciones habían firmado, entre ellas Suhrkamp, Hanser, Rowohlt, Carlsen, Penguin Random House Verlagsgruppe, Diogenes, la International Publishers Association y la Federation of European Publishers, además de editoriales de Brasil, Egipto, el Reino Unido (UK), Austria, Países Bajos, Argentina, Tailandia y Australia.

ja.headline:
出版団体150以上が
AI透明性の訴えに賛同
ja.body: Frankfurt AppealはEUとドイツにAI開発者へ学習作品の開示義務化を求める。

blocks.x: 150を超える出版社と出版団体が、EUとドイツ政府に対し、AI開発者にモデルの学習に使った作品の開示を義務づけるよう求めている。この要求は、ドイツ出版・書店協会が公表したFrankfurt Appealにまとめられている。

協会のSebastian Guggolz会長は「政治が今動かなければ、AIは私たちから何百万もの著作物を、そしてやがては考える力さえも奪い続けるだろう」と述べた。

zh.headline:
逾150家出版机构
联署AI透明度呼吁
zh.body: Frankfurt Appeal呼吁EU和德国要求AI开发者公开用于训练模型的作品。

blocks.x: 150多家出版商和出版组织正敦促EU和德国政府，要求AI开发者公开用于训练其模型的作品。这一诉求载于德国出版商与书商协会发布的Frankfurt Appeal中。
呼吁书提出三项行动：包括在作品层面公开训练数据在内的透明度义务；具备公平收益模式的授权市场；以及遵守欧洲著作权法，并配备有力的执行手段。“侵权而无须承担后果的权利毫无价值。”

es.headline:
Más de 150 grupos editoriales
piden transparencia en la AI
es.body: El Frankfurt Appeal pide a la EU y a Alemania que los desarrolladores de AI revelen las obras con las que entrenan.
es.mini_headline: El Frankfurt Appeal por la transparencia en AI

blocks.x: Más de 150 editoriales y organizaciones del sector instan a la EU y al Gobierno alemán a obligar a los desarrolladores de AI a revelar las obras usadas para entrenar sus modelos. La petición se recoge en el Frankfurt Appeal, publicado por la Asociación Alemana de Editores y Libreros.

El llamamiento pide tres medidas: obligaciones de transparencia que incluyan la divulgación de los datos de entrenamiento obra por obra; un mercado de licencias con modelos de ingresos justos; y el cumplimiento de la legislación europea de derechos de autor, con mecanismos sólidos para hacerla valer. “Los derechos cuya infracción no tiene consecuencias no valen nada”.

“Si los políticos no actúan ahora, la AI seguirá privándonos de millones de obras protegidas por derechos de autor y, con el tiempo, de nuestra capacidad de pensar”, afirmó Sebastian Guggolz, presidente de la asociación.

A 9 de octubre de 2026, más de 150 organizaciones habían firmado, entre ellas Suhrkamp, Hanser, Rowohlt, Carlsen, Penguin Random House Verlagsgruppe, Diogenes, la International Publishers Association y la Federation of European Publishers, además de editoriales de Brasil, Egipto, el Reino Unido (UK), Austria, Países Bajos, Argentina, Tailandia y Australia.

cards.headline:
AI 기업의 책 사냥에
Türkiye 저작권 우려
cards.body: 튀르키예 출판계는 AI 기업의 무단 스캔을 경계하면서도 라이선스 수익을 기대한다.

blocks.x: AI 기업들이 저작권료를 내지 않고 책을 상업용 모델 학습에 쓰면서 Türkiye 출판업계 전반에 우려가 번지고 있다. Türkiye 언론출판협회 Halil Celik 회장이 Anadolu Agency에 밝힌 바로는, 어떤 책이 AI 모델 학습에 쓰였는지 출판사가 확인할 믿을 만한 방법이 없다.
AI 기업들이 인쇄본을 대량으로 사들여 스캔한 뒤 실물을 폐기한다는 의혹이 나오면서 논란이 커졌다. Celik은 희귀본과 절판본, 그중에서도 마지막 남은 사본까지 해체하면 문화유산이 위태로워진다고 경고했다.
그는 Türkiye의 지식·예술저작물법을 고쳐 AI 학습, 데이터셋 공개, 처벌 규정을 넣어야 한다고 촉구했다. 단체 협약으로도 이용할 수 있는 라이선스 제도를 도입해 AI 기업이 상업적 이용의 대가를 치르게 하자는 제안도 내놓았다.
Celik은 “올바른 법·라이선스 체계가 갖춰지면 오늘 무료로 쓰이는 콘텐츠가 내일은 저작권과 라이선스 수익의 새로운 원천이 될 수 있다”고 말했다.

en.headline:
AI firms' book hunt stirs
copyright fears in Türkiye
en.body: Turkish publishers say AI firms scanning books without permission threaten copyright, yet some see licensing revenue.

blocks.x: AI companies’ use of books to train commercial models without paying copyright fees has raised concerns across Türkiye’s publishing industry. Halil Celik, president of Türkiye’s Press and Publishing Association, told Anadolu Agency that publishers have no reliable way of finding out which books have been used to train AI models.

The debate intensified after allegations that AI companies buy printed books in bulk, scan them and destroy the physical copies. Celik warned that dismantling rare and out-of-print books, some among the last surviving copies, puts cultural heritage at risk.

He called for amendments to Türkiye’s Law on Intellectual and Artistic Works, including rules on AI training, dataset disclosure and penalties, and proposed a licensing system, potentially through collective agreements, under which AI companies would pay for commercial use.
“If the right legal and licensing system is established, content that is used free of charge today could become a new source of copyright and licensing revenue tomorrow,” Celik said.

ja.headline:
AI企業の書籍漁りに
Türkiyeで著作権懸念
ja.body: トルコ出版界はAI企業の無断スキャンを著作権の脅威とみる一方、ライセンス収入も見込む。

blocks.x: AI企業が著作権料を払わずに書籍を商用モデルの学習に使っていることに、Türkiyeの出版業界全体で懸念が広がっている。Türkiye報道出版協会のHalil Celik会長はAnadolu Agencyに対し、どの書籍がAIモデルの学習に使われたかを出版社が確かめる確実な手段はないと語った。
AI企業が印刷本を大量に買い集めてスキャンし、現物を廃棄しているとの疑惑が出たことで、議論は激しさを増した。Celikは、現存する最後の数冊に数えられるものも含む希少本や絶版本を解体することは、文化遺産を危険にさらすと警告した。
同氏はAI学習、データセットの開示、罰則に関する規定を盛り込むよう、Türkiyeの知的・芸術的著作物法の改正を求めた。さらに、集団協定を通じた形も含め、AI企業が商用利用の対価を支払うライセンス制度を提案した。
「適切な法制度とライセンス制度が整えば、今日無料で使われているコンテンツが、明日には著作権とライセンス収入の新たな源泉になり得る」とCelikは述べた。

zh.headline:
AI公司大肆搜书
引发Türkiye版权担忧
zh.body: 土耳其出版界认为AI公司未经许可扫描图书威胁版权，但也有人看到授权收入。

blocks.x: AI公司未支付版权费便用图书训练商业模型，在Türkiye出版业引发普遍担忧。Türkiye新闻出版协会主席Halil Celik对Anadolu Agency表示，出版商没有可靠的办法查明哪些书被用来训练AI模型。
有指控称AI公司大批购买印刷图书，扫描后销毁实体书，争论随之升温。Celik警告称，拆解珍本和绝版书（其中一些是仅存的最后几册）会让文化遗产面临风险。
他呼吁修订Türkiye的《知识与艺术作品法》，纳入有关AI训练、数据集披露和处罚的规定，并提议建立一套许可制度（可能通过集体协议实现），让AI公司为商业使用付费。
Celik表示：“如果建立起合适的法律和授权体系，今天被免费使用的内容，明天就可能成为版权和授权收入的新来源。”

es.headline:
La caza de libros de la AI
alarma por derechos en Türkiye
es.body: Editoriales turcas ven en el escaneo de libros sin permiso por la AI una amenaza, pero también ingresos por licencias.
es.mini_headline: La caza de libros de la AI llega a Türkiye

blocks.x: El uso de libros por parte de empresas de AI para entrenar modelos comerciales sin pagar derechos de autor ha generado preocupación en todo el sector editorial de Türkiye. Halil Celik, presidente de la Asociación de Prensa y Edición de Türkiye, dijo a Anadolu Agency que las editoriales no tienen una forma fiable de saber qué libros se han usado para entrenar modelos de AI.

El debate se intensificó tras las acusaciones de que las empresas de AI compran libros impresos al por mayor, los escanean y destruyen los ejemplares físicos. Celik advirtió que desmontar libros raros y descatalogados, algunos de ellos entre los últimos ejemplares que se conservan, pone en riesgo el patrimonio cultural.

청취자 절반가량

en.headline:

are open to AI narration
en.body: An Audible-commissioned NielsenIQ survey in 11 markets finds audiobooks lead listeners back to print and e-books.

blocks.x: A global survey commissioned by Audible, “The Future of Listening,” was conducted by NielsenIQ and polled 18,000 consumers in 11 markets, including the U.S., U.K., several European countries, Japan and Brazil. Some 34% said they had listened to more audiobooks over the past year than in the previous one.

Some 69% of listeners had already read the title they listened to, and 63% who discovered an author in audio went on to buy another work by them. “Audiobooks are not competitive to other formats,” said Audible’s chief content officer Rachel Ghiazza.

About half of respondents said they would try AI narration, with interest higher for fiction than nonfiction in most markets, except Germany and Japan. Ghiazza called it “an and strategy”: human performers remain, and production savings are meant to fund more titles. “Quality and transparency are critically important.”
Audible has not detailed the survey’s methodology, but Ghiazza’s message to hesitant publishers was blunt: “The time is now.”

acepta la narración con AI
es.body: Una encuesta de NielsenIQ encargada por Audible en 11 mercados halla que el audio lleva a leer en papel y en digital.
es.mini_headline: Oyentes abiertos a las voces de AI

Cerca de la mitad de los encuestados dijo que probaría la narración con AI, con más interés por la ficción que por la no ficción en la mayoría de los mercados, salvo Alemania y Japón. Audible no ha detallado la metodología de la encuesta, pero el mensaje de Ghiazza a las editoriales indecisas fue tajante: “El momento es ahora”.
